title: Multi-vendor LLM integration
subtitle: Three frontier model families and local open-weight models run side by side in my programs, through subscription sessions, API seats and my own GPUs, with a terms-of-service firewall deciding which traffic may go where.

stats.label: a temporary client stays pending, because some assistants never register again
frontier model families whose tools and apps come in through one flow

lede: Auth and access plane had to let several vendors' assistants into one private tool estate: the command-line tools and desktop apps of three frontier model families, an agentic IDE and Microsoft Copilot Studio. Each behaves differently within what the standards allow. I set the pending-client lifetime from how real assistants behave, after watching clients cache an ID and never return. See The hardening fix that locked everyone out. FAFOHive needs a language model for background work: turning session activity into observations, writing summaries and narrating proven code paths. I did not want that work tied to one vendor, so I wrote one provider interface, and the memory pipeline stays vendor-neutral behind it.
quote: I decided to keep one authorization flow and move every vendor difference into a client profile held in configuration.
evidence: OAuth and identity architecture: one authorization flow for assistants from 3 frontier model families, an agentic IDE and Copilot Studio, vendor differences held in client profiles.
Multi-vendor LLM integration: 5 language-model providers behind one interface, any of them replaceable by a local OpenAI-compatible server with no change to callers.
Resilient API clients: one retry policy that backs off on transport, rate-limit and server errors and returns authentication, bad-request and parse errors at once.
author: Corey James
